First listed: 2026-10-02 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Why Private Equity's Software Bet Is Going to Zero | The Weekly Wrap](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xqRKETRfPM) - 2026-10-02
- [Substack: Why Private Equity's Software Bet Is Going to Zero | The Weekly Wrap](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/why-private-equitys-software-bet) - 2026-10-02

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman links FICO's loss of exclusivity to regulator antagonism and examines software buyouts financed in a low-rate era. His residual-equity example is arithmetically sound if enterprise value halves and debt is unchanged, but it does not establish that public equity drawdowns proxy private enterprise values. The precise refinancing cash demand is not a mathematical necessity. He also distinguishes oil supply shocks from the Fed's broader inflation role and describes the vintage-delinquency work behind his crisis trade.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

### 016. For a $1 billion buyout with unchanged $500 million debt, a fall in enterprise value to $500 million eliminates residual equity even if operations remain profitable.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 14:00-15:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xqRKETRfPM&t=840s) | Stance: conditional | Horizon: not stated

This conditional relationship follows from the stated assumptions; it does not establish that the assumptions hold empirically.

Conditional reasoning: Equity = max(EV - debt, 0) = zero. Operating profitability does not prevent valuation compression.

Assessment test: Verify EV and debt premises before applying to any real company.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

- [The Changing Sensitivity of Interest Rates to Oil Supply News](https://www.frbsf.org/research-and-insights/publications/economic-letter/2025/12/changing-sensitivity-of-interest-rates-to-oil-supply-news/) (2025-12): Oil supply shocks create inflation-growth tradeoffs; policy can dampen activity and expectations, and oil-price responses reflect both supply and demand.

## Framework and tools

- Model residual equity and refinancing explicitly.
- Distinguish operating performance from multiples.
- Use vintage credit data rather than stories to identify deterioration.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Five software buyout purchase prices and debt ratios
- Adobe public-share-price proxy
- Hypothetical 2027 refinancing waterfall
- Moody's securitization vintage database
